identity.name: GARWARE HI-TECH FILMS LTD
identity.industry: Specialty Polymer Films & Surface Protection Solutions

summary.oneLiner: Garware Hi-Tech delivered record Q4/FY26 profitability (EBITDA margin 26.2%) driven by operational leverage and product mix, while guiding for ~18% revenue growth in FY27 backed by a new INR191cr sun-control line and aggressive D2C studio expansion. The key catalyst remains the potential accounting benefit from US tariff refunds and imminent anti-dumping duties on Chinese/Korean imports.

one-line thesis: Garware Hi-Tech delivered record Q4/FY26 profitability (EBITDA margin 26.2%) driven by operational leverage and product mix, while guiding for ~18% revenue growth in FY27 backed by a new INR191cr sun-control line and aggressive D2C studio expansion. The key catalyst remains the potential accounting benefit from US tariff refunds and imminent anti-dumping duties on Chinese/Korean imports.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR597cr (Q4, +8.9% YoY), INR2,120cr (FY26, flat vs FY25 due to tariffs). EBITDA: INR157cr (Q4, +29% YoY, 26.2% margin); INR500cr (FY26, 23.6% margin). PAT: INR108cr (Q4, +39% YoY); INR338cr (FY26, 16% margin). Order Book: PPF lines at 85-89% utilization; Sun Control at 75-80%. Net Debt: Zero (Cash & liquid investments INR774cr). One-offs: FY26 revenue suppressed by 50% US tariffs; Q4 benefited from inventory release post-tariff resolution.
guidance: Revenue: Minimum INR2,500cr for FY27 (~18% growth). Margin: 25% +/- 2% (EBITDA). Order Inflow: Strong visibility with PPF/Sun Control lines nearing full utilization. Capex: INR191cr new sun-control line (commissioning June 2027); TPU line commissioning Oct 2026.
order book & pipeline: PPF utilization 85-89%; Sun Control utilization 75-80%; Expected full utilization by FY27 end; New sun-control line adds 1,200 lakh sq ft capacity.
segment / subsidiary detail: Sun Control: ~50% of revenue (Architectural ~25% of SCF). PPF: ~25% of revenue. IPD/Commodity: ~25% of revenue. D2C mix: 10-15% global, ~40% domestic PPF.
growth verticals / optionality: Garware Home Solutions targeting INR200cr revenue by FY28; 50 D2C studios by FY27 end; Middle East subsidiary targeting $20-22mn (25-30% CAGR); TPU backward integration improving margins.
margins & cost dynamics: D2C margins 25-30% higher than B2B; Raw material (PTA/MEG) hikes largely passed through; 45-50% natural hedge on currency via import parity raw materials.
capex / expansion: INR191cr for new automated sun-control line (new facility, operational Q1 FY28); Previous INR500cr+ spent on 2 PPF, 1 sun control, 1 metalizer, 1 TPU lines (fully funded by internal accruals).
capital allocation: Debt-free balance sheet with INR774cr cash; All capex funded via internal accruals; Focus on high-ROI D2C infrastructure and capacity expansion.
risks & watch-items: Delay in US tariff refund accounting; Geopolitical disruption in Middle East shipping routes; Raw material volatility (PTA/MEG); Execution risk on 50-studio D2C rollout.
management quality / tone: Confident and aggressive on volume growth; Disciplined on capital allocation; Transparent on tariff headwinds; Bullish on D2C margin expansion.
non-obvious takeaways: Sun-control line expansion prioritized over PPF due to higher fungibility (can produce PPF if needed) and larger absolute capacity addition (125 lakh sq ft/month vs 25 lakh for PPF); Architectural films growing faster than automotive due to 'privacy on demand' (PDLC) adoption.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

themes.title: Specialty packaging & sustainable materials
themes.need: Premiumization, e-commerce and a sustainability/recycling mandate drive a packaging up-cycle across flexible films, rigid plastics, cartons and compostables. UFLEX/EPL/HUHTAMAKI/COSMOFIRST/ESTER on films/tubes; TCPLPACK/AGI/BOROLTD on cartons/glass; MOLDTKPAC/MOLDTECH on rigid/IML; PAKKA/GANECOS on compostable & recycled materials.
themes.driver: Brand-owner restocking; export demand recovery; recycled-content mandates; commodity-cost pass-through.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Described as a "Leading global manufacturer of hi-tech, value-added specialty films" with "Fully integrated chips-to-film operations" and a "Diverse, customized portfolio of 3,000+ SKUs".
- Claims the "World's largest single-location SCF capacity" (elsewhere phrased "One of World's largest Single-location SCF capacity") and to be "India's only producer of professional-grade PPF".
- Premium brand claim: "A premium global brand, ranking top 3 in USA & Europe"; the 'Global' and 'Garware' brands "target the high-end market", with the economy segment "mainly dominated by Chinese and Korean players".
- "Leading player in India's shrink film market with ~70% market share"; "Extensive Global distribution network with presence across 90+ countries".
- IP/moat markers: "Over 10 Registered/Pending Patents and 168 Registered Trademarks"; proprietary nano-dispersion technology for NIR blocking films; JIPM award; Gold Shield from the Government of India.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Medium-term outlook] For "FY27 & Beyond" the deck sets out Revenue CAGR 15-20%, EBITDA Margin 23-27%, Export Share 70%+ and VAP contribution 85%+, caveated "The actual numbers might vary as per the change in Macro-economic situation".
- [Achieved base] The corresponding "FY18 to FY26" block shows Revenue ₹2,120 Cr, EBITDA Margin 23.6%, Export Share 75% and VAP contribution 87%.
- [Internal contradiction] Revenue CAGR is stated as "Revenue CAGR 17%* (FY21-FY26)" on one slide while a footnote on the same page reads "*FY21-25 Revenue CAGR 21%" — both readings are reproduced here rather than reconciled.
- [Export/domestic mix] Export vs domestic split shown as 73%/27% (FY22), 70%/30%, 78%/22%, 77%/23%, 75%/25% (FY26).
- [Certification framing] Every slide footer carries "A GreenPro Certified company".
